major_events: In [第001章 星空中的青铜巨棺], a class reunion at Mount Tai is interrupted when nine giant dragon corpses pulling a bronze coffin crash into the summit, trapping Ye Fan and his classmates inside.
In [第012章 荧惑], the bronze coffin lands on Mars, where the passengers disembark and explore the ancient desert ruins of the Great Thunder Temple (大雷音寺), retrieving ancient Buddhist relics.
In [第020章 鳄祖], the ancient demon Crocodile Ancestor (鳄祖) awakens on Mars and unleashes small crocodile beasts that attack the group, causing several casualties before the survivors escape.
In [第027章 荒古禁], the bronze coffin arrives at the Big Dipper star region and lands inside the Barren Ancient Forbidden Area (荒古禁地).

In [第032章 弹指红颜老], the characters realize they have rapidly aged into old men and women after exiting the Forbidden Area, while Ye Fan and Pang Bo have transformed into younger children due to eating the divine fruits.

In [第037章 灵墟洞天], Ye Fan and Pang Bo are taken to the Lingxu Sect (灵墟洞天), where Ye Fan's body is identified as the Ancient Sacred Body (荒古圣体) but deemed unsuitable for cultivation under current worldly laws.
In [第055章 妖帝坟冢], the tomb of the last Demon Emperor opens in the ancient ruins, attracting human cultivators and demon beasts to fight for the Emperor's treasures.

In [第065章 神秘绿铜], Ye Fan secretly obtains a mysterious piece of green copper and a golden book containing the Wheel-Sea volume of the Dao Scripture (《道经》) during the chaotic struggle at the Demon Emperor's Tomb.
In [第093章 炼人为药], Elder Han (韩长老) captures Ye Fan and tries to refine him into medicine inside a furnace, but Ye Fan uses the green copper piece and his golden bitter sea to kill Han and escape.
In [第118章 颜如玉], Ye Fan encounters the Demon Princess Yan Ruyu and is temporarily held by the demon race who try to use his Sacred Body to nurture the Demon Emperor's heart.
In [第123章 青铜仙殿], Ye Fan and Ji Ziyue are trapped inside the legendary Bronze Celestial Palace beneath the lake but escape with the Mother Qi of All Things (万物母气).
In [第135章 秘术现世], at Zhuo Peak (拙峰) of Taixuan Sect, the declining inheritance of the peak is revived, and Ye Fan successfully obtains the "Jie" character secret (皆字秘) of the Nine Secrets.
In [第149章 大能——孔雀王], the powerful Demon King Kongque Wang attacks the Ji family's stronghold to avenge the demon race, shaking the Southern Region and forcing Ye Fan to flee.
In [第176章 横渡北域], Ye Fan escapes the Ji family's relentless pursuit by utilizing a domain teleportation portal to relocate to the resource-rich Northern Region.
In [第192章 神王姜太虚], inside the Purple Mountain, Ye Fan meets the trapped Peerless God King of the Jiang Family, Jiang Taixu, who has been stuck for 4,000 years and is near death.
In [第193章 神王传法], Jiang Taixu passes down the "Dou" character secret (斗字秘) of the Nine Secrets, the supreme attack technique, to Ye Fan before Ye Fan searches for the Source Book.
In [第196章 无始经], Ye Fan discovers the scripture left by Emperor Wushi (无始大帝) inside Purple Mountain, but cannot open it because he lacks the required emperor's jade keys.
In [第208章 五千年攻击第一（上）], Ye Fan enters Pingyan City and uses the methods of the Source Book to engage in high-stakes stone gambling, winning rare treasures and drawing attention from major sects.
character_state_transitions: Ye Fan (叶凡): From a mortal graduate with no cultivation abilities in [第001章 星空中的青铜巨棺] to an active cultivator with a golden Bitter Sea (金色苦海) in [第046章 金色的苦海].

Ye Fan (叶凡): From a rejuvenated young boy to an aged old man with white hair due to the life-draining curse of the holy mountain in [第107章 登上圣山], then restored back to youth after taking the sacred medicine in [第111章 神桥境界].
Ye Fan (叶凡): From a Wheel-Sea (轮海) realm cultivator at the Bitter Sea (苦海) stage in [第041章 开辟苦海] to a breakthrough to the Spring of Life (命泉) stage in [第097章 晋升命泉境界].
Ye Fan (叶凡): From a Spring of Life (命泉) stage cultivator to the Divine Bridge (神桥) stage in [第111章 神桥境界].
Ye Fan (叶凡): From a Divine Bridge (神桥) stage cultivator to the Bridge's Peak/Bridge Crossing (彼岸) stage in [第164章 跃海登彼岸].
Pang Bo (庞博): From a loyal human classmate and Lingxu disciple in [第037章 灵墟洞天] to being possessed and controlled by the ancient demon soul of the Demon Emperor's descendant in [第059章 妖帝之心].

Li Ruoyu (李若愚): From a silent, seemingly ordinary old gatekeeper of the declined Zhuo Peak in [第133章 大成若缺] to a powerful master who comprehends the natural Dao and successfully inherits the peak's legacy in [第136章 自然大道].
Elder Han (韩长老): From an influential elder of Lingxu Sect searching for longevity herbs in [第053章 韩长老] to a dead cultivator killed inside his own refining furnace by Ye Fan in [第093章 炼人为药].

Ji Ziyue (姬紫月): From an arrogant and witty princess of the Ji Family who looks down on Ye Fan in [第101章 鼎威] to a cooperative travel companion who trusts Ye Fan and shares secrets after surviving the Bronze Celestial Palace in [第127章 玄黄].

Jiang Taixu (姜太虚): From the glorious, peerless God King of the Jiang family in historical lore to a withered, dying captive trapped inside the stone walls of Purple Mountain for 4,000 years in [第192章 神王姜太虚].

Yao Xi (摇光圣女): An aloof, powerful and holy virgin of Yaoguang Holy Land who attempts to capture Ye Fan in [第172章 掀翻圣女] to a humbled captive stripped of her defensive undergarment (the silver metal chest protector) in [第173章 洞房] and [第174章 禽兽亦或不如].

Zhang Wuye (张五爷): From a simple old village chief of a desolate oasis who is bullied by local bandits in [第177章 流血乱地] to a respected guide who passes down his ancestral stone armor and directs Ye Fan to enter Purple Mountain to find the Source Book in [第184章 源天师] and [第186章 天书].

long_form_mechanisms.name: The Wheel-Sea Cultivation Realm (轮海秘境)
long_form_mechanisms.description: The first major cultivation secret realm of the body, which contains four sub-stages: opening the Bitter Sea (苦海), establishing the Spring of Life (命泉), building the Divine Bridge (神桥), and crossing to the Other Shore (彼岸). Cited in [第074章 四大境界] and [第164章 跃海登彼岸].

long_form_mechanisms.name: The Ancient Sacred Body (荒古圣体)
long_form_mechanisms.description: A legendary human physique that was once invincible but is now considered useless because its Bitter Sea is solid and cannot be easily activated, requiring astronomical amounts of resources (like "Source") to advance. Cited in [第036章 荒古圣体] and [第075章 体若无底洞].

long_form_mechanisms.name: The Nine Secrets (九秘)
long_form_mechanisms.description: Nine supreme, ancient secret techniques created by nine different Mythical Era Emperors, each representing the pinnacle of a specific domain (e.g. "Jie" 皆 for multiplying power, "Dou" 斗 for attack). In this chunk, Ye Fan obtains the "Jie" secret at Zhuo Peak and the "Dou" secret from Jiang Taixu. Cited in [第132章 九秘之一] and [第193章 神王传法].

long_form_mechanisms.name: Source Master Techniques (源术)
long_form_mechanisms.description: The art of identifying, selecting, and cutting raw stones containing "Source" (the crystallized essence of cosmic energy) from ancient mines. It involves reading geological formations and avoiding dangerous curses or ancient creatures trapped inside stones. Cited in [第184章 源天师] and [第199章 源术].

long_form_mechanisms.name: Mother Qi of All Things (万物母气)
long_form_mechanisms.description: The primordial essence of the universe, extremely heavy and rare, which Ye Fan obtains from the Bronze Celestial Palace and uses to forge his personal weapon (器) in the shape of a tripod cauldron. Cited in [第127章 玄黄] and [第098章 一器破万法].

long_form_mechanisms.name: The Vision "Sea Rising Bright Moon" (海上生明月)
long_form_mechanisms.description: A rare and powerful visual manifestation of inner cultivation (异象) possessed by special physiques like the East Wasteland God Body (东荒神体) of Ji Haoyue, which project a cosmic scene to suppress enemies. Cited in [第120章 东荒神体] and [第122章 苦海种金莲].

long_form_mechanisms.name: Demon Emperor's Tomb Activation (妖帝坟冢开启)
long_form_mechanisms.description: The process by which the tomb of the Demon Emperor emerges from the hot spring, separating into the Yang tomb (holding the emperor's weapon and heart) and the Yin tomb (containing his actual corpse), attracting rival factions. Cited in [第055章 妖帝坟冢] and [第066章 阳墓与阴坟].

long_form_mechanisms.name: The Life-Draining Force of the Forbidden Area (荒古禁地剥夺生命力)
long_form_mechanisms.description: The environmental hazard of the Barren Ancient Forbidden Area, where the "荒" (Desolation) force rapidly drains the vitality and age of any living beings who enter, causing them to wither into old age unless they consume the divine fruits. Cited in [第034章 荒之传说] and [第107章 登上圣山].

continuity_observations: The mysterious bronze coffin (九龙拉棺) is introduced in [第001章 星空中的青铜巨棺] as the vehicle that brings Ye Fan to the Big Dipper, and it reappears in [第103章 青铜巨棺又现] when it crashes back down in the Barren Ancient Forbidden Area, showing a persistent connection to the main storyline.

The Bodhi seed (菩提子), retrieved by Ye Fan from the Great Thunder Temple on Mars in [第015章 菩提], is carried by him continuously and plays a critical role in helping him comprehend the Golden Book of the Dao Scripture in [第073章 借菩提观道经].

The mysterious green copper piece (神秘绿铜) obtained by Ye Fan from the Demon Emperor's Tomb in [第065章 神秘绿铜] resides in his Bitter Sea and acts as a passive shield, repeatedly protecting him from extreme dangers, such as the Demon Emperor's heart in [第119章 绿铜镇圣心] and the deadly force of the Bronze Celestial Palace in [第123章 青铜仙殿].

The rivalry between Ye Fan and Bixia/Lingxu disciples (especially the descendants of Elder Han) starts in [第053章 韩长老] and reaches its climax when Elder Han attempts to refine Ye Fan in [第093章 炼人为药], resolving that specific subplot while establishing Ye Fan's reputation.

The character of Li Xiaoman, Ye Fan's ex-girlfriend, is introduced on Earth in [第005章 李小曼], travels with him to the Big Dipper, joins the Ziyang Sect, and their complex, distant relationship is maintained in [第087章 相逢李小曼] and [第088章 淡然相对].

The legend of the Nine Secrets (九秘) is first introduced as a scattered set of supreme techniques, and Ye Fan's quest to gather them is established when he obtains the first one ("Jie") at Taixuan Sect in [第132章 九秘之一] and the second one ("Dou") in Purple Mountain in [第193章 神王传法].

The curse of the Source Heavenly Master (源天师的可怕晚年) is introduced by Zhang Wuye in [第189章 源天师的可怕晚年] as a tragic fate that awaits all who practice advanced Source techniques, setting up a long-term threat and mystery for Ye Fan's future character development.

The Emperor's Jade (帝玉) is introduced as a mysterious relic in [第187章 帝玉] which Ye Fan obtains, and it is later shown to be related to the 无始经 (Wu Shi Jing) in Purple Mountain in [第196章 无始经] and [第211章 又见无始], serving as a plot device that links different locations and relics.
style_observations: Escalation of Conflict via Sect Hierarchies: The narrative structures conflicts around hierarchical power groups. Ye Fan starts by fighting minor disciples, then elders (Elder Han), then young geniuses (Ji Haoyue, Yao Xi), and finally powerful demon kings and holy land lords. Cited in [第030章 阿猫阿狗], [第093章 炼人为药], and [第149章 大能——孔雀王].

Contrast of Protagonist's Non-Conformist Attitude: The author frequently contrasts Ye Fan's calm, sarcastic, or modern Earth-based pragmatic attitude with the solemn, traditional, and arrogant behavior of the local cultivators, generating humor and dramatic irony. Cited in [第088章 淡然相对] and [[第173章 洞房].

Vivid Environmental and Sensory Descriptions during breakthroughs: Breakthroughs and spellcasting are accompanied by highly detailed, colorful, and destructive visual metaphors (such as golden waves, roaring seas, and starry skies). Cited in [第046章 金色的苦海] and [第122章 苦海种金莲].

Interweaving of Chinese Mythological and Philosophical Concepts: The text extensively incorporates elements of traditional Taoist cosmology (such as the Yin-Yang balance, the concepts of "Dao", and the five elements) and Buddhist relics into the cultivation system and naming conventions. Cited in [第014章 大雷音寺], [第040章 道经], and [第136章 自然大道].

Serialized Cliffhangers and Foreshadowing: Chapters frequently end with suspenseful revelations, new threats, or high-stakes confrontations to keep the reader engaged in a serialized format. Cited in [第085章 危机来临] and [第148章 捅破天].

Use of Abstract Visions to Represent Combat Strength: The author represents the combat capabilities of elite cultivators not just through physical speed or raw energy, but through poetic and conceptual "visions" (异象) like "Sea Rising Bright Moon" or "Bitter Sea Cultivating Golden Lotus". Cited in [第120章 东荒神体] and [第122章 苦海种金莲].

creation_family_evidence.author: 辰东 (Chen Dong)
key_concepts: 九龙拉棺 (Nine Dragons Pulling the Coffin)

creation_family_evidence.stylistic_signature: Features grand-scale cosmic introductions (like the nine dragon corpses and bronze coffin traveling through space), deep integration of ancient Chinese mythology and Taoist concepts, high-stakes stone gambling (赌石) systems in the Northern Region, and powerful visual manifestations/visions (异象) in combat. The narrative style is typical of Chen Dong's works, characterized by massive world-building, high-octane battles, and a blend of modern humor with ancient fantasy concepts.
creation_family_evidence.compilation_indicators: The chapter headers are formatted as '第XXX章 Title' (e.g., '第001章 星空中的青铜巨棺') with three-digit numbers, which is typical of serialized web novels from platforms like Qidian, compiled and formatted for local offline readers.

originality_risks: The Overused Rejuvenation/Aging Plot Device: The trope of having characters enter a forbidden area and lose their age, only for the protagonist to gain a special body and later reverse the process, is a common fantasy shortcut to establish early power dynamics and unique status. Cited in [第032章 弹指红颜老] and [第111章 神桥境界].

The "Trash Physique" which is actually Invincible: The trope of the protagonist possessing a physique (Ancient Sacred Body) that is widely deemed useless by the current era's experts, yet turns out to be the most powerful once the protagonist overcomes a specific, resource-heavy obstacle, is a standard underdog narrative structure. Cited in [第036章 荒古圣体] and [第075章 体若无底洞].

The Unscrupulous and Greedy Comic Relief Companion: The introduction of Duan De as a fat, greedy, tomb-robbing Taoist who acts as a minor antagonist and occasional ally is a highly standard xianxia character archetype designed to provide comic relief and contrast with the protagonist. Cited in [第063章 无良道士] and [第173章 洞房].

Dividing Cultivation into Highly Rigid Linear Stages: The strict progression of cultivation stages (Bitter Sea, Spring of Life, Divine Bridge, Other Shore) with detailed technical breakthroughs aligns closely with the standardized progression structures popularized in the web novel era, which can reduce narrative flexibility. Cited in [第074章 四大境界] and [第164章 跃海登彼岸].
